info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package compliance is your KYC/KYB onboarding, accreditation records, and the evidence trail behind them.

get.summary: Returns the org's tracked accreditation-state records, newest first — evidence entries the org keeps, never a platform certification.
get.description:
Returns the org's tracked accreditation-state records, newest
first — evidence entries the org keeps, never a platform certification.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit caps the rows returned; non-positive means the server default.

post.summary: Records an ASSERTED accreditation state for a subject — the subject's own assertion, with no verifier.
post.description:
Records an ASSERTED accreditation state for a subject — the
subject's own assertion, with no verifier. Every CONFIRMED state
(provider_verified, reviewer_confirmed) and every rejected/expired state is a
DECISION recorded via the decision endpoint, attributed to the reviewer — a
create can never stamp a confirmation. The underlying figures (income, net
worth) are never stored; only the method, category, and state.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the accreditation record to read, from the path.

post.summary: Records an org reviewer's decision on an accreditation record — a reviewer confirmation, a provider verification the reviewer has evidence of (a CPA/attorney letter, a verifier report), a rejection, or an expiry.
post.description:
Records an org reviewer's decision on an accreditation
record — a reviewer confirmation, a provider verification the reviewer has
evidence of (a CPA/attorney letter, a verifier report), a rejection, or an
expiry. ROLE-GATED (an org admin or platform reviewer) and ATTRIBUTED: the
reviewer's identity is recorded as ReviewerSub and audited. Human-in-the-loop:
the platform never confirms on its own, and even a provider_verified state
carries the reviewer who recorded it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the accreditation record to decide, from the path.

get.summary: AuditRead is the compliance read of the SHARED tamper-evident audit plane — the SOC 2 posture surface (privileged actions: who started/decided what, when).
get.description:
AuditRead is the compliance read of the SHARED tamper-evident audit plane —
the SOC 2 posture surface (privileged actions: who started/decided what, when). The
org is PINNED to the caller's validated org and the rows are narrowed to
compliance.* actions. Fail-closed: no principal is a 403, no configured audit
store a 501.

parameters.name: result
parameters.description: Result filters rows by outcome result: success, deny, or error; empty means all.

get.summary: Health reports subsystem liveness and the wired verification provider.
get.description:
Health reports subsystem liveness and the wired verification provider. Fail-open
on purpose: it never probes the external provider, so a provider outage cannot
fail liveness.

get.summary: ListRecords is the unified compliance-record view for the org: its verifications and accreditation records together, each provider-reported or tracked, never platform-asserted.
get.description:
ListRecords is the unified compliance-record view for the org: its verifications
and accreditation records together, each provider-reported or tracked, never
platform-asserted. PII stays in the subject store; records carry only opaque ids
and statuses.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit caps the rows returned; non-positive means the server default.

get.summary: Status is the org's honest posture read: the wired provider and the per-status tally of its verifications.
get.description:
Status is the org's honest posture read: the wired provider and the per-status
tally of its verifications. It is deliberately NOT a boolean "compliant" — it
reports counts of provider-reported states and carries the boundary disclaimer.

get.summary: Returns the org's subjects as PII-MINIMIZED summaries — no name or email, only whether an email is on file.
get.description:
Returns the org's subjects as PII-MINIMIZED summaries — no name or
email, only whether an email is on file. The full record is returned only by the
explicit single-subject read.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit caps the rows returned; non-positive means the server default.

post.summary: Records a party the org is verifying as part of its own onboarding/compliance — a team member, vendor, customer, or counterparty.
post.description:
Records a party the org is verifying as part of its own
onboarding/compliance — a team member, vendor, customer, or counterparty. The
subject's contact PII (name/email) is sealed at rest and returned only to the
owning org; downstream records reference the subject by opaque id.

get.summary: Returns one subject WITH its contact PII — the only surface that returns it, and only to the owning org.
get.description:
Returns one subject WITH its contact PII — the only surface that
returns it, and only to the owning org. The response is never cached by any
intermediary.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the subject to read, from the path.

get.summary: Returns the org's KYC/KYB verifications, newest first — opaque subject references and provider-reported statuses only, no subject PII.
get.description:
Returns the org's KYC/KYB verifications, newest first — opaque
subject references and provider-reported statuses only, no subject PII.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit caps the rows returned; non-positive means the server default.

post.summary: Begins a KYC/KYB verification of a subject through the wired provider — an existing subject by id, or one created inline from the request.
post.description:
Begins a KYC/KYB verification of a subject through the wired
provider — an existing subject by id, or one created inline from the request.
The returned status is provider-reported and never terminal on a fresh start:
starting a verification can never yield a verified record, and a provider error
is a 502, never a verification.

post.summary: Provider push that settles a verification, authenticated by HMAC signature
post.description:
The external PUSH reconcile: a verification provider (or a Hanzo relay) signals that a check settled, and the reconciled check comes back. It authenticates by an HMAC SIGNATURE over the RAW body bytes rather than by a principal — an external caller has no validated org — and the org is then resolved FROM the record the signed provider reference matches, so a call can only ever touch the one tenant that owns that reference.

The body carries NO trusted decision. A valid signature cannot force a status: the reference only says WHICH check to re-read, and the status is then pulled from the wired provider, which stays the source of truth. With no real provider configured a check stays pending, and the only route to a passing status is the role-gated, attributed reviewer decision.

An unknown reference is a benign 200 `{"ignored": ...}` no-op, not an error, so a provider replaying stale events neither retry-storms nor learns whether a reference exists in some other tenant. Fails closed otherwise: 501 unless a webhook secret is configured, 401 on a signature that does not verify, 400 with no provider reference, 413 over 1 MiB, and 502 if the secret or the provider is unreachable.

get.summary: Returns one verification — its opaque subject reference and provider-reported status, no subject PII.
get.description:
Returns one verification — its opaque subject reference and
provider-reported status, no subject PII.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the verification to act on, from the path.

post.summary: Records a privileged reviewer's MANUAL decision on a verification — the human-in-the-loop path, and the ONLY route to a passing status when no real provider is wired.
post.description:
Records a privileged reviewer's MANUAL decision on a
verification — the human-in-the-loop path, and the ONLY route to a passing status
when no real provider is wired. It produces a DISTINCT reviewer_confirmed, never
a provider_verified (a provider decision is the provider's to report, via the
webhook or a reconcile), and it is ROLE-GATED (an org admin or platform reviewer)
AND ATTRIBUTED (the reviewer's user id is DecidedBy), so a manual pass is always
accountable.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the verification to decide, from the path.

post.summary: Polls the wired provider for its current decision and records it, ATTRIBUTED to the provider — the internal PULL reconcile.
post.description:
Polls the wired provider for its current decision and
records it, ATTRIBUTED to the provider — the internal PULL reconcile. For the
Manual provider the check stays pending; for a hosted provider it reflects the
provider's settled status. A poll error is a 502, never a verification.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the verification to act on, from the path.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt is when the subject was first recorded, Unix SECONDS.

email.description:
Email is the party's address, when the org supplied one. It is PII: sealed at
rest, returned only to the owning org, and never copied into a check record.

id.description:
ID is the opaque handle every other record uses to point at this party. It is
the only reference that leaves this type, which is what keeps the PII in one
place: a check, an accreditation and an audit row all carry the id and none of
them carry the name.

kind.description:
Kind is what is being verified: "individual" (a natural person, so KYC) or
"business" (a legal entity, so KYB). It decides which provider flow runs.

name.description:
Name is the party's name, under the same PII rule as Email. For a business it
is the legal entity name rather than a trading name, since that is what a
provider verifies against.

org.description:
Org is the tenant that is doing the verifying — the party who must answer for
this record, not the party being verified. A subject is returned only to it.

ref.description:
Ref is the org's OWN identifier for this party, carried so a caller can match a
subject back to their system without keeping a second mapping. Opaque here:
nothing in this plane parses or enforces it.

updatedAt.description:
UpdatedAt is when the subject's own fields last changed, Unix seconds. A check
moving to a new status does not touch it — that history lives on the check.

action.description:
Action is the verb that was performed. It is the event's name, not the HTTP
method — a request-sourced record carries both, and the pair is what makes a
row readable ("grant.create" at POST /v1/admin/grants).

authMethod.description: Auth is the credential the actor presented: "jwt", "api-key", or "none".

email.description:
Email is the actor's validated address, absent when the credential carried
none. It comes from the verified token, never from a client header.

hash.description:
Hash is this record's SHA-256 over its own canonical JSON with both hash
fields cleared, folded with prevHash. Recomputing it from the row's other
fields is what proves the row has not been edited.

home.description:
Home is present ONLY on a cross-org action: the org the actor came FROM,
while Org is the org they acted IN. A console row carrying `home` is a
platform-admin impersonation and should be rendered as one.

isAdmin.description:
IsAdmin is the VALIDATED platform-SuperAdmin bit at decision time (membership
of the reserved admin org), never the client's own claim to be one.

method.description:
Method is the HTTP verb, on a record a request produced. Absent on an event
emitted from inside the binary with no request behind it.

org.description:
Org is the tenant the action was taken IN — the effective org, which for
everyone but an impersonating SuperAdmin is also the actor's own. Empty on an
unauthenticated request.

path.description:
Path is the request's route. Any segment shaped like a credential is replaced
before the record is written, so a key that rides in a path is not preserved
here by the very control meant to watch it.

prevHash.description:
PrevHash is the hash of record seq-1, which is what links the rows into a
chain: a deleted or reordered record breaks the recomputation at that point.
The first record of a chain carries 64 zeros rather than an empty string, so
"start of chain" and "field missing" cannot look alike.

reason.description:
Reason is a short explanation for a deny or an error ("SuperAdmin required",
"insufficient_balance"). It is never a secret and never a raw upstream error
body; absent on a success.

requestId.description:
RequestID ties this row to the request-line log and any downstream trace — the
X-Request-Id the pipeline minted for that request.

resource.description:
Resource is the KIND of thing acted upon ("org", "role", "secret",
"provider-config", "credit"). Where a mutation has no finer semantics than its
route, this is the route family and resourceId is empty — the action and the
path already pin the object.

resourceId.description: ResourceID is the specific instance, absent when the kind alone identifies it.

result.description:
Result is how the action ended: "success", "deny" or "error". A deny is a
decision this binary made and is as much evidence as a success.

seq.description:
Seq is the record's position in the chain, 0-based and gapless. The Recorder
assigns it under its own lock, so it is a true total order: seq n+1 was
written after seq n, and a missing number is a missing record.

sourceIp.description:
SourceIP is the client address the edge resolved for the request, after the
proxy chain — the address a responder would act on, not the socket peer.

status.description:
Status is the HTTP status the caller received. It is the outcome as the client
saw it, so a 200 carrying a domain refusal still reads 200 here.

sub.description:
Sub is the acting user (the IAM subject). Empty for a machine principal or an
anonymous request, which is how a service action is told from a person's.

time.description:
Time is when the action happened, RFC3339Nano in UTC. The stored column has
the same precision and sorts the same way, so a client can range and order on
this string verbatim.

userAgent.description:
UserAgent is the client the request announced itself as. Client-supplied, so
it is evidence about what claimed to act, not proof of it.

total.description: Total is the sum over every status.

bearer.description: The caller's credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is either an access token minted by Hanzo IAM or an API key (pk-/sk-). X-Authorization, and HTTP Basic carrying the token as the password, are accepted spellings of the same header for clients that cannot set Authorization; a browser presents the session cookie instead. Every operation requires it unless it says `security: []`.
